questions.q: Two metal spheres of radius $R$ and $3 R$ have same surface charge density $\sigma$. If they are brought in contact and then separated, the surface charge density on smaller and bigger sphere becomes $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$, respectively. The ratio $\frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}$ is.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For conducting sphere, $\mathrm{V}=\frac{\sigma \mathrm{r}}{\varepsilon_0}$
After contact, $\mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{V}_2$
$\begin{aligned}
& \sigma_1 r_1=\sigma_2 r_2 \\ & \frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}=\frac{r_2}{\mathrm{r}_1} \\ & \frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}=3
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An electric charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is placed at origin <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></math> co-ordinate system. Two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> are situated at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> respectively. The potential difference between the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the potential difference between P and Q is given by

∆V=kq1r1-1r2   ...1

Now,

r1=(3)2+(3)2 m=6 m

And,

r2=(6)2+0 m=6 m

As r1=r2=6 m and the value of the charge remains constant, the potential difference between the points is zero.

questions.q: A dipole comprises of two charged particles of identical magnitude q and opposite in nature. The mass m of the positive charged particle is half of the mass of the negative charged particle. The two charges are separated by a distance l . If the dipole is placed in a uniform electric field E→; in such a way that dipole axis makes a very small angle with the electric field, E→. The angular frequency of the oscillations of the dipole when released is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The data given is 

l=distance between the charges

q=charge

m=mass of the positive charge

2m=mass of negative charge 

The moment of inertia of the system is 

I=m×2mm+2ml2=2ml23

The angular frequency can be written as 

ω=pEI   ...(i)

Substituting the value of moment of inertia in the equation (i) we get 

ω=pE2ml23=3pE2ml2

The value of the dipole moment is

p=ql

Hence, the angular frequency becomes

ω=3qE2ml

This question was given bonus by NTA as none of the options matched in the original paper.

questions.q: Two identical metallic spheres <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> when placed at certain distance in air repel each other with a force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math>. Another identical uncharged sphere <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is first placed in contact with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and then in contact with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> and finally placed at midpoint between spheres <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math>. The force experienced by sphere <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let charge on A and B be qA=qB=q.

Then force acting between them is F=Kq2r2.

When C is placed in contact with A, charge on A and C will be =q2

Now C is placed in contact with B, charge on B  and C will be =q+q22=3q4

Now, force experienced by sphere C is 

F'=F2-F1=K9q216×r24-K3q28×r24=K3q4-Kq2r24×3q4

=3Kq24r2=3 F4

questions.q: Four point charges <math><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></math> and <math><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></math> are placed on y-axis at <math><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo>,</mo></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo>,</mo></math> respectively. The magnitude of the electric field <math><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></math> at a point on the x-axis at <math><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mo>,</mo></math> with <math><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mo>≫</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo>,</mo></math> will behave as:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The electric field at P is superposition of the fields due to all four charges. The electric field due to the two +q charges is

E+q=KqD2+d2cos⁡θ1×2
E-q=KqD2+4d2cos⁡θ2×2
The field due to +q is towards right and the field due to -q is towards left. Also θ1≈0 and θ2≈0 .
∴Enet=E+q-E-q≈KqD2+d2-KqD2+4d2
=Kq 3d2D2+d2D2+4d2≈3Kqd2D4
E∝1D4

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Net dipole moment of a polar linear isotropic dielectric substance is not zero even in the absence of an external electric field.
Reason (R) : In absence of an external electric field, the different permanent dipoles of a polar dielectric substance are oriented in random directions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: (A) is correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not correct
Both $(\mathrm{A})$ and $(\mathrm{R})$ are correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A : Since polar dielectrics are randomly oriental $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}_{\mathrm{net}}=\overrightarrow{0}$.
R : If $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}$ is absent, polar dielectric remain polar \& are randomly oriented.

questions.q: A vertical electric field of magnitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> just prevents a water droplet of a mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> from falling. The value of charge on the droplet will be : (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
To balance gravitational force, electric force on the liquid drop should act in upward direction.

For translational equilibrium along vertical direction,

qE=mg

⇒q=mgE=0.1×10-3×9.84.9×105=2.0×10-9C

questions.q: Four equal point charges <math><mi>Q</mi></math> each are placed in the <math><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></math> plane at <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> . The work required to put a fifth charge <math><mi>Q</mi></math> at the origin of the coordinate system will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done in bringing the fifth charge at origin is equal to change in the potential energy of the system of charges.

Wext=ΔU=Uf-Ui if Ui=0 (assumed)

Wext=Uf-0=KQ22+KQ22+KQ225+KQ225

Hence, the work done in bringing the fifth charge at the origin is 
Wext=Q24πε01+15.

questions.q: If two charges <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> are separated with distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> and placed in a medium of dielectric constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math>. What will be the equivalent distance between charges in air for the same electrostatic force?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The force between the two charges when they are placed in dielectric is

F1=14πεokq1q2 d2

The force between the two charges when they are placed at separation d' is

F2=14πεoq1q2 d'2 

Since, the force between the two charges is same in both case

F1=F2

⇒14πεok     q1q2 d2= 14πεo q1q2 d'2

⇒d'=dk

Separation between the plates is 0.5 mm. If the dipole is rotated by $30^{\circ}$ from the axis, it tends to realign in the direction due to a torque. The value of torque is :

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{~d}}=\frac{5}{5 \times 10^{-4}}=10^4 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m} \\ & \tau=\mathrm{PE} \sin \theta
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An infinitely long positively charged straight thread has a linear charge density $\lambda \mathrm{Cm}^{-1}$. An electron revolves along a circular path having axis along the length of the wire. The graph that correctly represents the variation of the kinetic energy of electron as a function of radius of circular path from the wire is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric field $\mathrm{E}$ at a distance $\mathrm{r}$ due to infinite long wire is $E=\frac{2 k \lambda}{r}$ Force of electron $\Rightarrow F=e E\begin{aligned} & F=e\left(\frac{2 k \lambda}{r}\right) \\ & F=\frac{2 k \lambda e}{r} \end{aligned}$
This force will provide required centripetal force $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{F} & =\frac{\mathrm{m}^2}{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{r}} \\ \mathrm{v} & =\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}} \\ \mathrm{KE} & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}\right) \\ & =\mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: An electric dipole of dipole moment is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> placed in a uniform electric field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in such a way that dipole moment is along electric field. The work done in rotating dipole by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo> </mo></math>in this field will be_______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mJ</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work done for rotating a dipole is given by the change in the potential energy. The potential energy is given by

U=-p→·E→

W =∆U = Uf−Ui

So, the work done is 

 W=-pEcos180°-(-pEcos0°)=2pE=2×6×10-6×1.5×103=18 mJ

questions.q:
A 1 m long copper wire carries a current of 1 A. If the cross section of the wire is 2.0 mm2 and the resistivity of copper is 1.7×10-8 Ω m. The force experienced by moving electron in the wire is _____×10-23 N

(Charge of electron=1.6×10-19C )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, length l=1 m, current i=1 A, area A=2×10-6 m and resistivity ρ=1.7×10-8 Ω m.

Resistance of wire is R=ρlA=1.7×10-8×12×10-5=1.72×10-2 Ω

Now, electric field in the wire is E=ρJ, where, J=iA is current density.

Thus, E=iρA=iR=1×1.72×10-2 V m-1

Electric force in terms of electric field is given by F=qE

Therefore, force experienced by moving electron is F=1.6×10-19×1.72×10-2

=1.36×10-21=136×10-23 N

questions.q: At the centre of a half ring of radius $\mathrm{R}=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ and linear charge density $4 \mathrm{n} \mathrm{C} \mathrm{m}^{-1}$, the potential is $x \pi \mathrm{V}$. The value of $x$ is _______
questions.subject: Physics

Potential at centre of half ring
$\begin{aligned} & V=\frac{K Q}{R} \\ & V=\frac{K \lambda \pi R}{R} \\ & V=K \lambda \pi \Rightarrow V=9 \times 10^9 \times 4 \times 10^{-9} \pi \\ & V=36 \pi\end{aligned}$
